newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Weak on low Taiwan award, thin demand.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Weak on low Taiwan award, thin demand.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices were steady to soft on very thin demand and a low award to Taiwan's latest buy tender, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Traders quoted prices for free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting April in a wide range of $260 to $270 per tonne, compared to $265-$270 last week.
"It is not easy to gauge because it is very quiet," said a producer.
One trader said he bought an April lifting parcel as low as $260 fob Singapore from producer.
"It is getting progressively weaker. The producers are the ones pushing down the market...look at the tenders awarded," a trader said.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) on Tuesday bought through tender 3,500 tonnes of MTBE for May 6-20 delivery between $275 to $280 per tonne, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Kaohsiung and Keelung, a company official said.

The tender which closed March 31, was awarded at a lower price than CPC's last tender where it bought 7,000 tonnes for April 6-20 delivery from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) at a higher $280-$283 per tonne c-and-f Kaohsiung and Keelung.
One South Korean petrochemical company sold an end March 1,500 tonnes lifting mid-April at $270 per tonne fob Korea to Japan.
"The price is high because it is a very small volume," the source said. "But two producers in South Korea are only operating at 80 percent because of low prices in Asia."
He said Hyundai Petrochemical Co which produces 100,000 tonnes per year and Daelim which produces 140,000 tonnes per year had cut runs in mid-March.
"We are thinking about the manufacturing costs...we can't export at these prices," he said.
But Daelim will not have any more export availabilities due to its plant's maintenance shutdown from May 1-22.
Traders expected Asian prices find support at around $255 fob Singapore, the level which opens up the arbitrage to the U.S..
